title: Playlist-driven open-fit + bench mapping demo
next_steps: Redwood to send playbook export + bench template (Lena)
VectorGrid to share 1 week of anonymized latency token traces (Marta)
Schedule 1hr pilot kickoff with Dedicated sizing (Diego)
Set up trial account and run 3-model bench using provided runner (Emily)
action_items: Lena: email playbook export and bench spreadsheet by 2028-05-11
Diego: prepare recommended Dedicated sizing and cost estimate by 2028-05-12
Marta: provide latency and QPS traces (anonymized) by 2028-05-13
Emily: confirm pilot internal stakeholders and timeline by 2028-05-14
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked VectorGrid through a playlist-driven workflow for selecting open models, mapping them to bench cases and compatibility matrices. Focus: production-fit (latency/cost), fallback branches, and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Okay, everyone, thanks for joining. We're at 2 PM Pacific, I'm Lena, AE on the account, with Diego, our SE. Do you all see the demo deck I just shared? link: https://redwood.app/decks/playlist-demo
[00:23] Emily (VectorGrid): Yep, we can see it. Thanks, Lena. Raghu had to step in from another meeting but he's here now.
[00:37] Diego (Redwood): Great, quick agenda — show the playlist-driven picklist, map to bench cases, then compatibility matrix and routing rules, and finish with a suggested Dedicated sizing. We'll keep it practical.
[00:58] Raghu (VectorGrid): Quick context — our product serves realtime scoring for recommendation microservices. Latency target 60ms p95, cost is sensitive, and we have some PII in features so VPC is attractive.
[01:18] Lena: Perfect, that helps. Do you currently run models in-host or in our cloud?
[01:26] Marta (VectorGrid): Right now it's mixed — internal models on-prem, a couple of vendor APIs for specific tasks. The handoff in prod is messy, so we're evaluating a unified inference layer.
[01:42] Diego: Ok, so the playlist concept helps pick candidate open models for each task and then run bench cases against them. Slide 4 shows the 'playlist' — think of it like a prioritized picklist: candidate models, intended workload, quant profiles, and dev notes.
[02:05] Jason (VectorGrid): Walk me through a real example — how do we go from model name to deployable variant?
[02:13] Diego: Sure. Example: we add 'ggml-open-7b' as candidate. The playlist records target seq len, quantization (e.g., 4-bit, LLM.int8), and an expected cost envelope. The bench runner will then test throughput/latency for your tail lat distribution and output a compatibility score.
[02:34] Emily: Are those bench runners runnable in our env or do they need Redwood infra?
[02:40] Diego: Both — we provide a lightweight bench runner you can run in your VPC or on a Redwood sandbox. It emits CSVs compatible with the compatibility matrix. You keep the traces if you want; we only ask for anonymized telemetry for sizing.
[02:58] Raghu: You mentioned compatibility score — what factors go into that?
[03:04] Diego: It's a weighted score: latency SLO hit rate, token throughput cost, GPU memory fit, kernel match (we report quant/kernel compatibility), and quality regression vs baseline. We show tradeoffs in the matrix.
[03:23] Lena: Quick note — quality testing is tied to your eval set; the playlist can pin a specific prompt set for regressions.
[03:33] Emily: Nice. Can we see the compatibility matrix UI?
[03:38] Diego: Yep, jumping to the console demo.
[03:44] [04:10] Diego: (screen) This is the matrix — rows are models, columns are bench cases and infra dims. The cells are color coded with hover to see details. Example, Open-7B-Int8 passes memory but p95 is 120ms on our 80-token bench, so it's amber for your 60ms target.
[04:35] Marta: Huh, that 120ms — is that measured on CPU or GPU?
[04:40] Diego: GPU; this sample was on an A10G equivalent. If you run it on a higher-end A100 or use quant kernels, that shifts. Also we show fallback variants — e.g., route to a trimmed 3B when p95 spikes.
[04:58] Emily: So routing policies can be per-endpoint?
[05:03] Diego: Exactly. Per-route routing — latency-first, cost-first, or canonical fallback. You can pin a primary model and two fallbacks.
[05:13] Raghu: Data residency — if we do VPC, do logs leave our network?
[05:18] Lena: For Redwood Private / Dedicated we support VPC tunnels and optional private control plane. Audit logs can stay in your KMS-backed storage. We also have SOC 2 + ISO docs; I'll send the security pack.
[05:33] Jason: Any caveats with KV cache across variants? We use heavy caching for session-based scoring.
[05:40] Diego: Good question. KV cache semantics are preserved if variants are compatible. The console flags lifetime and compatible tokenization. Sometimes quant changes require re-encoding; we flag that as a migration action.
[05:58] Emily: Can we try building a playlist for our 'rec-rerank' flow?
[06:04] Lena: Let's do that live — I'll create a new playlist called 'rec-rerank-v2'.
[06:12] [06:40] Diego: Adding candidates: open-3b, open-3b-quant, and open-7b-int8. Setting bench case: short-context rerank, 32 tokens, 500 QPS target, 60ms p95 target.
[07:05] Lena: Now we kick off bench mapping — this will create bench runs and expected infra matches. We can run in sandbox or generate recommended Dedicated sizing without running.
[07:20] Marta: Could the estimated sizing be way off? Our production has bursty QPS.
[07:27] Diego: The estimate is based on your pasted traces and the bench case distribution. For burstiness we recommend adding buffer and configuring autoscale with burst capacity; Dedicated supports buffer pools.
[07:45] Raghu: How do you handle fallback in case of model degradation — automatic failover?
[07:51] Diego: Yes, policy-driven. If p95 or error rate breaches threshold, route to fallback variant or fallback model in a different region. We also support staged canary and gradual rollbacks.
[08:05] Jason: Show us the bench results sample now if you can.
[08:10] Diego: Loading a recent bench. 
[08:18] [08:45] Diego: Here, you can see bench rows for each candidate: mean latency, p50/p95/p99, token cost, GPU util, and a quality delta against your baseline prompts. Notice open-3b hits p95 at 44ms and cost per 1k tokens is lower; open-7b-int8 gives better quality but higher latency.
[09:10] Emily: That quality delta — how stable is it across prompt types? We have three prompt families.
[09:17] Diego: You can break bench by prompt family; the playlist can attach multiple bench cases. In this demo I only had a single bench but you can pivot and see per-prompt scores.
[09:34] Lena: Also the Optimize tab will recommend quant profiles given a cost target. Sofia, wanna show that?
[09:41] Sofia (Product): Sure. Optimize uses historical bench data and your SLO to suggest quant + kernel combos. For example, for rec-rerank-v2, it recommends 4-bit LLM.int8-s variant on A10G to meet cost target, or 8-bit with layered kernel on A100 for latency headroom.
[10:05] Marta: Do those recommendations include fallbacks if the recommended kernel is unavailable?
[10:10] Sofia: Yes — we output alternative compatible kernels and a fallback plan. The compatibility matrix highlights kernel availability per infra.
[10:21] Raghu: Can we have different routing for different customers? We offer tiered SLAs.
[10:26] Diego: Absolutely — routing policies can be tenant-aware. You can route premium customers to low-latency clusters and economy to cost-optimized clusters.
[10:39] Emily: Security again — where are the embeddings stored if we enable caching?
[10:44] Lena: Cache and temporary artifacts can be configured to stay in your VPC storage, with envelope encryption via your KMS. We'll include the KMS integration doc.
[10:58] Jason: Any integrations for our observability stack? We use Datadog and Prometheus.
[11:03] Diego: We emit tracing hooks and Prometheus metrics; Datadog can ingest via exporter. You can see per-token latency traces in Console and export them.
[11:18] [11:40] Emily: Ok, a practical question: if we run the bench in our VPC and a model shows poor latency, can Redwood suggest a quantization config to try locally?
[11:49] Diego: Yes — the bench runner includes suggested quant transforms and a lightweight conversion script. For some models we also provide tuned kernels.
[12:02] Marta: Is there a workflow to promote a playlist candidate to production?
[12:07] Lena: Yes — playlist -> bench -> compatibility pass -> canary rollout. The console shows promotion buttons and required gate checks (perf, regressions, audit).
[12:19] Raghu: Let's talk cost — can you ballpark cost for Dedicated for our QPS?
[12:24] Diego: If you share the traces we'll generate a Dedicated sizing. From other customers with similar QPS we see X GPUs baseline; rough estimate: $Y/month. We'll send a tailored sheet.
[12:40] Jason: Is there a minimum commit for Dedicated?
[12:44] Lena: There's a reserved capacity commitment; we can flex on term for pilots. Details in the pricing sheet.
[12:52] [13:20] Diego: I want to highlight the 'compatibility reasons' tab — each amber/red cell has a note: e.g., kernel mismatch, memory oversubscription, tokenization drift, or quality regression. This helps narrow root cause rather than guess.
[13:42] Emily: Nice. Can the compatibility matrix be exported to CSV for our internal runbooks?
[13:47] Diego: Yes, export to CSV/JSON. And the playbook export includes bench configs so you can re-run.
[13:58] Marta: Are there examples of customers who used playlist -> bench and improved cost 20% while keeping latency?
[14:03] Lena: We have case studies — I'll link the frictionless migration case and a bench-driven 18% cost reduction for a microservice at scale.
[14:18] Raghu: One more on fallbacks: do you do cross-region fallback automatically? We need DR for regional outages.
[14:24] Diego: We support region-aware routing with health checks and automatic cross-region failover. It does increase egress; the console will estimate incremental cost.
[14:38] Emily: Let's talk pilot scope — we want to run a 2-week bench on three candidate models, and validate p95 on our traces.
[14:46] Lena: Great — proposed pilot: 2-week bench, run in your VPC using our bench runner, evaluate three models, provide Dedicated sizing and cost estimate, security packet and SOC docs.
[15:01] Jason: Timeline?
[15:04] Lena: If Marta shares traces by Monday, we can have bench configs and the pilot runner ready by Wednesday, run for 2 weeks, then checkpoint. Diego can lead the pilot kickoff.
[15:18] Diego: Sounds good. I'll draft the bench config template after the call.
[15:23] [15:45] Raghu: Thanks, this was useful. A couple of small things — can we whiteboard how quantization might impact tokenization for us specifically?
[15:52] Diego: Yes, we'll include a short tech note on tokenization and quant side effects.
[16:02] Emily: And please include an example bench CSV so our infra folks see the schema.
[16:08] Lena: Will do. I'll send the playbook export, bench template, and the security pack. Expect an email by Friday EOD.
[16:20] Marta: Thanks, everyone.
[16:23] Lena: Thanks all — we'll follow up with next steps.
[16:30] [END TRANSCRIPT]
